topic: Multi-intent task decomposition for LLM tool and skill routing
name: SkillRouter (2026)
description: SkillRouter (arXiv:2603.22455, Alibaba Group, 2026) is a two-stage retrieve-and-rerank skill-selection pipeline for LLM agents operating over very large skill registries (~80K skills). Its central empirical finding is that the skill body (full implementation text) is the decisive routing signal: removing it causes 29-44pp degradation across retrieval methods and cross-encoder attention concentrates 91.7% on the body field. Because agents cannot fit skill bodies in context (they see only name+description / progressive disclosure), the routing layer must have body access — an inherent router-agent information asymmetry. The compact 1.2B pipeline (SR-Emb-0.6B bi-encoder + SR-Rank-0.6B cross-encoder, both fine-tuned from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) hits 74.0% Hit@1, beating an 8B/16B zero-shot pipeline at 13x fewer params and ~5.8x faster, and runs on consumer hardware. This is the closest published match to the Labmate skill-routing problem.
decomposition_method: None — SkillRouter does not decompose the prompt. It treats the user task as a single query and routes it to the most relevant skill(s) from the registry. Multi-intent decomposition is out of scope; the contribution is selection accuracy over a large pool, not splitting compound prompts. [uncertain]
decomposition_granularity: Not applicable — no sub-task splitting; the unit is the whole task query mapped to a skill. [uncertain]
ordering_strategy: Not applicable — single-skill (or top-N) selection per query; no multi-step ordering or DAG is produced by the router. [uncertain]
decomposition_validation: Not applicable to decomposition (no decomposition step). The analogous quality control is selection validation via the cross-encoder reranker, plus training-time techniques: false-negative filtering (+4.0pp Hit@1, +3.1pp MRR@10) and listwise reranker training (pointwise collapses to 43.3% Hit@1 vs 74.0% listwise). [uncertain]
hierarchy_depth: flat — a flat ranked list of candidate skills from an ~80K registry; no milestone/step hierarchy or skill tree.
router_type: retrieve-then-rerank (two-stage). Stage 1: bi-encoder embedding retrieval (SR-Emb-0.6B) recalls top-20 candidates over the full skill text. Stage 2: cross-encoder reranker (SR-Rank-0.6B) jointly scores each (query, candidate) pair via cross-attention over full skill text, re-sorts, and returns top-1/top-N.
routing_model: Separate fine-tuned compact models (not the main agent LLM): SR-Emb-0.6B (bi-encoder, fine-tuned from Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) + SR-Rank-0.6B (cross-encoder reranker), 1.2B total. Embedding similarity for recall; learned cross-attention scoring for rerank. Compared against Qwen3-Emb/Rank 0.6B/8B and BM25 baselines.
handles_ambiguity: best-effort ranked pick. The reranker produces a refined relevance ordering and the system selects top-1 (or top-N for downstream planning); there is no clarification request, abstention, or POMDP-based disambiguation. Overlapping/ambiguous skills are handled by the cross-encoder's full-body scoring, which is why body access materially improves accuracy in high-overlap registries. [uncertain]
fallback_behavior: top-N pass-through to downstream planner. Rather than a hard error/abort, the pipeline can return the top-N shortlisted skills for downstream planning/execution when top-1 is uncertain; no explicit human escalation or re-decomposition is described. [uncertain]
skill_pool_scale_and_retrieval: two-stage (coarse bi-encoder recall + fine cross-encoder rerank) over ~80K skills — explicitly the 'thousands+ of skills' regime. Bi-encoder retrieves top-20; cross-encoder reranks on full skill body. Key finding: BM25 and name+description-only methods drop to near-zero / degrade below encoder-only (best nd rerank 33.3% vs 56.0% encoder-only) when bodies are excluded; full-body access is necessary, not optional.
router_agent_asymmetry: Yes — this is the paper's central insight. The router (encoder + reranker) sees the full skill body, while the executing agent sees only name+description (progressive disclosure, bodies too long for context). Removing the body costs 29-44pp across methods; 91.7% of cross-encoder attention falls on the body field. The routing layer therefore must hold information the agent itself never sees.
execution_pattern: Not an executor — SkillRouter is a selection/routing component upstream of execution. It outputs top-1/top-N skills that a downstream agent/planner then executes; the paper's end-to-end study wires it into four coding agents. [uncertain]
parallel_vs_concurrent: Not applicable — the router itself performs ranking, not tool execution; no parallel-vs-concurrent execution distinction is made. [uncertain]
dependency_detection: Not applicable — single-query skill selection; no inter-sub-task dependency analysis (no decomposition to analyze). [uncertain]
result_aggregation: Not applicable to multi-result merging — the router returns a ranked shortlist (top-1/top-N) rather than aggregating execution outputs. Stage outputs are combined as recall→rerank scores (yes/no relevance score sort). [uncertain]
mid_chain_feedback: none (within the router). The retrieve-then-rerank pipeline is a single forward pass per query with no mid-chain re-planning; any feedback loop would live in the downstream agent, not SkillRouter. [uncertain]
benchmark_name: SkillsBench (a SkillsBench-derived benchmark, ~80K candidate skills, ~75-query core set) plus SkillBench-Supp (independently built supplementary benchmark: 100 GT skills from 3 sources, 256 single-label queries over a 77K-skill pool). End-to-end study across four coding agents.
multi_intent_coverage: Single-intent / single-label selection. Benchmarks are single-label (one ground-truth skill per query); compound multi-intent prompts are not the focus. The hard dimension evaluated is scale and skill overlap, not parallel-vs-sequential multi-intent. [uncertain]
accuracy_metric: exact-match style ranking metrics: Hit@1 (top-1 routing accuracy) as primary, plus MRR@10 and NDCG@10. SkillRouter 1.2B = 74.0% Hit@1 vs 8B/16B Qwen3 base pipeline 68.0%; encoder-only 65.4%/56.0%; best 8B base encoder alone 64.0%.
clarification_capability: Not measured. SkillRouter does not model when-to-ask vs. when-to-answer or generate clarification questions; it is a pure selection/ranking system. [uncertain]
process_vs_outcome_eval: outcome-style ranking evaluation (Hit@1/MRR/NDCG on selecting the correct skill), plus an end-to-end task-success study; no intermediate process-supervision scoring of a multi-step plan.
eval_stability: Reproducible offline benchmark: fixed skill registries (~77-80K skills) and released models/eval scripts on GitHub/HuggingFace; not dependent on live external APIs, so numbers are reproducible (avoids the StableToolBench-style API-drift problem). [uncertain]
integration_pattern: standalone routing service/component upstream of the agent: retrieve top-20 with SkillRouter-Embedding-0.6B, rerank with SkillRouter-Reranker-0.6B, return top-1/top-N for downstream planning/execution. Demonstrated wired into four coding agents; lightweight enough for consumer-hardware deployment.
routing_layer: application-layer (a dedicated retrieval+rerank layer between user task and agent execution); not pushed into the inference engine. Architecturally a separate sub-1.2B routing tier. [uncertain]
latency_overhead: Low and explicitly optimized: the compact 1.2B pipeline runs ~5.8x faster than the strongest base (8B/16B) pipeline at 13x fewer parameters, and bi-encoder recall (top-20) before expensive cross-encoder scoring keeps the rerank cost bounded to a small candidate set — deployable on consumer hardware.
online_adaptation: static — models are fine-tuned offline (false-negative-filtered, listwise reranker training) and deployed fixed; no production-feedback bandit/RL adaptation described. Generalization is shown via held-out SkillBench-Supp without re-tuning. [uncertain]
adoption: open-source (with code and models): GitHub zhengyanzhao1997/SkillRouter; HuggingFace pipizhao/SkillRouter-Embedding-0.6B and SkillRouter-Reranker-0.6B; benchmark + eval scripts released. Research paper (Alibaba Group, 2026); no commercial API confirmed.
